tags.name: Measurement Sessions
tags.description:
Manual, canvas-based BOQ measurement — an additive flow that runs alongside
(and independently of) the spreadsheet-style Takeoff flow.

---

## Overview

A **measurement session** is opened against an uploaded drawing. Users draw
measurement elements directly on a canvas (counting piles, measuring lengths,
areas, rebar bends, etc.). Sessions are **resumable** — a user can close the
tab and come back later to continue on the same drawing. Sessions may be
**collaborative**: multiple project members can join the same session over
Socket.IO and see each other's cursors and element changes in real time.

When measuring is complete, the session is **finalized** — its elements are
materialized into `TakeoffElement`s and (optionally) run through the existing
takeoff commit to produce a BOQ. The underlying takeoff / BOQ engine is reused
unchanged.

---

## Access control

Every endpoint is scoped to a project. A caller may access a session when they
are either the **project owner** or an **active project member**. Finalization
materializes elements under the project owner's account so existing takeoff
ownership rules continue to apply.

---

## Calibration & measurement

Geometry points are stored in **canvas pixels**. A `calibration` reference
(a line of known real-world length + its pixel length) derives `scale`
(real-world units per pixel). The server recomputes lengths/areas
authoritatively; if calibration changes, all existing elements are recomputed.

---

## Realtime (Socket.IO)

Connect with a JWT (`auth.token`) and use these events (rooms are keyed
`measurement:<sessionId>`):

| Event (client → server)          | Payload                                   | Effect                                   |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `measurement:join`               | `{ sessionId }`                           | Join room; returns session + elements    |
| `measurement:leave`              | `{ sessionId }`                           | Leave room                               |
| `measurement:cursor`             | `{ sessionId, x, y }`                     | Broadcast cursor (ephemeral, not saved)  |
| `measurement:element:upsert`     | `{ sessionId, element }`                  | Persist + broadcast element              |
| `measurement:element:delete`     | `{ sessionId, clientId }`                 | Delete + broadcast                       |
| `measurement:canvas`             | `{ sessionId, canvas }`                   | Persist + broadcast canvas/calibration   |

Server → client: `measurement:presence`, `measurement:cursor`,
`measurement:element:upserted`, `measurement:element:deleted`,
`measurement:canvas:updated`, `measurement:error`.

---

## Frontend flow

```
1. POST  /uploads                                     Upload the drawing
2. POST  /projects/:projectId/measurement-sessions    Open (or resume) a session
3. Socket measurement:join                            Join for realtime collab
4. draw → measurement:element:upsert / REST elements  Persist measurements
5. GET   /measurement-sessions/:id                    Re-hydrate on return
6. POST  /measurement-sessions/:id/finalize           Prepare the BOQ
```

tags.name: Multi-File BOQ (RAG)
tags.description:
AI-powered Bill of Quantities generation from **multiple BIM and/or PDF files**
combined via RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) using vector search.

Unlike the single-file BIM and PDF BOQ pipelines, this endpoint accepts
**a mix of BIM (RVT, IFC, DWG, etc.) and PDF files** in one request.
All files are processed in parallel, their data is embedded into a vector
store, and Claude generates a unified BOQ by semantically searching across
all source data.

---

## When to Use Multi-File vs Single-File

| Scenario | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Single BIM/CAD file with no PDFs | **BIM Pipeline** (`/api/v1/bim/`) |
| Single PDF drawing | **PDF BOQ** (`/api/v1/pdf-boq/`) |
| Multiple BIM files (e.g. Architectural + Structural + MEP) | **Multi-File BOQ** (`/api/v1/boq/`) |
| Mix of BIM + PDF specification docs | **Multi-File BOQ** |
| BIM model + PDF bill of materials | **Multi-File BOQ** |

---

## Supported File Types

| Extension | Category | Format |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| `.rvt`    | BIM      | Autodesk Revit |
| `.ifc`    | BIM      | Industry Foundation Classes |
| `.dwg`    | BIM/CAD  | AutoCAD Drawing |
| `.dxf`    | BIM/CAD  | Drawing Exchange Format |
| `.nwd`    | BIM      | Navisworks Document |
| `.dgn`    | BIM/CAD  | MicroStation Design |
| `.skp`    | BIM      | SketchUp |
| `.obj`    | BIM      | Wavefront OBJ |
| `.fbx`    | BIM      | Autodesk FBX |
| `.3dm`    | BIM      | Rhino 3D Model |
| `.stp`/`.step` | BIM | STEP CAD Exchange |
| `.sat`    | BIM      | ACIS SAT |
| `.f3d`    | BIM      | Fusion 360 |
| `.pdf`    | PDF      | PDF Drawing / Specification |

---

## Frontend Integration Guide

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. POST /multi-generate       Upload files → get jobId      │
│         ↓                                                    │
│  2. GET /multi-jobs/:jobId     Poll every 5-10s              │
│         ↓ (status === "completed")                           │
│  3. Display BOQ from data.result                             │
│         ↓                                                    │
│  4. (Optional) PATCH /multi-jobs/:jobId    Save user edits   │
│  5. (Optional) GET /multi-jobs/:jobId/pdf  Download PDF      │
│  6. (Optional) POST /multi-jobs/:jobId/create-project        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Frontend pseudo-code:

```javascript
// 1. Upload multiple files
const formData = new FormData();
files.forEach(f => formData.append('files', f));
formData.append('documentHint', 'Mixed-use residential + commercial, 8 floors, Abuja');
const upload = await POST('/boq/multi-generate', formData);  // multipart
const jobId = upload.data.jobId;

// 2. Poll job status
let result;
do {
  await sleep(5000);
  result = await GET(`/boq/multi-jobs/${jobId}`);
} while (['pending', 'extracting', 'embedding', 'generating'].includes(result.data.status));
if (result.data.status !== 'completed') throw new Error(result.data.errorMessage);

// 3. Display the BOQ
displayBoq(result.data.result);

// 4-6. Same as single-file flows
```

---

## Processing Stages

| Status       | What's Happening |
|-------------|------------------|
| `pending`    | Job queued, files received |
| `extracting` | BIM files translating via APS; PDFs being read by Claude Vision |
| `embedding`  | Extracted data being vectorized via Voyage AI embeddings |
| `generating` | Claude generating unified BOQ via RAG (vector search) |
| `completed`  | ✅ BOQ ready |
| `failed`     | ❌ Error — check `errorMessage` |

---

## Limits

- **Max files:** 20 per request
- **Max file size:** 200 MB per file (BIM) / 32 MB (PDF)
- **Accepted formats:** BIM + PDF (see table above)
- **Job expiry:** 7 days (create a project to persist permanently)

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Project lifecycle — create, configure, and manage QS projects.

---

## Overview

A **Project** is the top-level entity that groups all quantity surveying work.
It is created via `POST /projects` and then enriched through a multi-step
setup wizard before the user enters the takeoff workspace.

---

## Manual-Mode Project Setup Wizard

For `processingMode: manual` projects, the frontend walks the user through
these steps (each backed by a dedicated endpoint):

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Step 1 — POST /projects                                            │
│           Create the project (name, source, processingMode, etc.)    │
│                          ↓                                          │
│  Step 2 — PATCH /takeoff/{projectId}/qs-config                      │
│           Select QS project type, foundation types, swimming pool,   │
│           number of floors, lift option, global rebar/concrete       │
│           defaults (see Takeoff tag for full docs)                   │
│                          ↓                                          │
│  Step 3 — PUT /takeoff/{projectId}/structural-scope/{foundationType}│
│           Configure structural scope per foundation type             │
│           (see Structural Scope tag for full docs)                   │
│                          ↓                                          │
│  Step 4 — PATCH /projects/{projectId}/finishing                      │
│           Set finishing specs, floor & wall tile types               │
│                          ↓                                          │
│  Step 5 — PATCH /projects/{projectId}/metrics                       │
│           Set financial metrics (markup, retention, contingency)     │
│                          ↓                                          │
│  Workspace — Takeoff element CRUD + calculation (Takeoff tag)        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Other endpoints in this tag

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /projects/{id}` | General-purpose update (metadata, status, client info, dashboard fields) |
| `POST /projects/{id}/boq/save-to-library` | Promote a BOQ row to a library item |
| `PATCH /projects/{id}/archive` | Soft-archive (reversible, blocks mutations) |
| `DELETE /projects/{id}` | Permanent deletion (owner only, irreversible) |
| `GET /projects/{id}/dashboard` | Computed project dashboard summary |
| `GET /projects/{id}/activity` | Recent project activity feed |

---

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Default — project is being set up |
| `active` | Project is in use |
| `archived` | Soft-archived — read-only, no mutations allowed |

---

## Error Handling

| HTTP | Condition |
|---|---|
| 400 | Validation error (bad enum, missing required field) |
| 401 | Missing or expired JWT token |
| 403 | Caller lacks access, or project is archived |
| 404 | Project not found or not owned by the user |

tags.name: Structural Scope
tags.description:
Per-foundation-type material and construction configuration for manual-mode projects.

---

## Overview

The Structural Scope module captures material specs, casting methods, and formwork
details for each foundation type selected on the project. It is Step 3 of the
manual-mode project wizard and feeds into the takeoff calculation engine.

Each foundation type gets its own scope document keyed by `{projectId, foundationType}`.
The visible tabs depend on the foundation type:

| Foundation Type              | Available Tabs                                                        |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `pile`                       | Pile System & Concrete Details, Superstructure                        |
| `raft`                       | Superstructure                                                        |
| `strip`                      | Superstructure                                                        |
| `raft_pile_with_basement`    | Pile System & Concrete Details, Blinding, Substructure, Superstructure|

---

## Data Sections

- **Pile Specification**: Concrete grade, casting method, pile dimensions, rebar details.
  Only relevant for `pile` and `raft_pile_with_basement` foundation types.
- **Blinding Elements**: Per-element blinding layer configuration (grade, thickness, waste).
  Only relevant for `raft_pile_with_basement`.
- **Substructure Filling**: Total filling, laterite, and hardcore thickness + waste.
  Only relevant for `raft_pile_with_basement`.
- **Substructure Elements**: Per-element concrete, formwork, waterproofing config.
  Only relevant for `raft_pile_with_basement`.
- **Superstructure Elements**: Per-element concrete, casting, waterproofing config.
  Relevant for all foundation types except `piling_alone` projects.
- **Finishing Elements**: Per-element concrete, casting, waterproofing config for finishing works.
  Relevant for all foundation types.

---

## Frontend Integration

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. User selects foundation type in Step 2 (QS Config)                  │
│         ↓                                                               │
│  2. GET /:projectId/structural-scope/:foundationType                    │
│         → Load saved scope config (or start fresh if 404)               │
│         ↓                                                               │
│  3. User fills in tabs (Pile System, Blinding, Substructure, etc.)      │
│         ↓                                                               │
│  4. PUT /:projectId/structural-scope/:foundationType                    │
│         → Save/update the entire scope config for that foundation type  │
│         ↓ (repeat per foundation type)                                  │
│                                                                         │
│  5. GET /:projectId/structural-scope                                    │
│         → List all saved scope configs (summary view)                   │
│                                                                         │
│  6. DELETE /:projectId/structural-scope/:foundationType                 │
│         → Remove a scope config (e.g., user removes a foundation type)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Error Handling

| HTTP | Condition                                                              |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 400  | Invalid foundation type, validation error                              |
| 401  | Missing or expired JWT token                                           |
| 403  | Project is archived — no mutations allowed                              |
| 404  | Project not found, scope not found, or foundation type not on project  |

post.description:
Accepts a multipart file upload and kicks off Autodesk Platform Services (APS) translation.

**What happens:**
1. File is uploaded to the APS Object Storage Service (OSS) transient bucket.
2. An SVF2 translation job is started (both 2D and 3D views are requested).
3. The Base64 URL-safe **URN** is returned — **store this value**, you need it for all subsequent calls.

**File size limit:** 200 MB  
**Supported formats:** RVT, DWG, DXF, IFC, NWD, DGN, SKP, OBJ, FBX  
**Rejected formats:** PDF (use `/api/v1/pdf-boq/generate` instead)

> **Frontend note:** Also save `req.file.originalname` (the uploaded filename).

post.summary: Step 3 — Submit BIM BOQ generation job (async)
post.description:
Kicks off the property-extraction + Claude AI reasoning pipeline in the background
and returns a `jobId` immediately (**HTTP 202**).

**Prerequisites:** Only call this endpoint after `GET /status/:urn` returns `status === "success"`.

**Background pipeline (runs automatically):**
1. **2D/3D Detection** — Determines if the file is a 2D CAD drawing or 3D BIM model,
   using the `originalFilename` extension and APS manifest derivatives.
2. **View selection** — For 3D BIM: prefers `{3D}` views. For 2D CAD: prefers layout/plan views.
3. **Property extraction** — Fetches all element properties from the selected view (with auto-retry).
4. **Format-specific filtering:**
   - **3D BIM (RVT/IFC/NWD):** Groups by Category, extracts Family/Type Name, trusts native units.
   - **2D CAD (DWG/DXF/DGN):** Groups by Layer, applies mm→m conversion, extracts hatch patterns.
5. **Claude AI reasoning** — Claude (quantity surveyor prompt) generates a structured BOQ.
6. **Thumbnail** — Fetches the APS model thumbnail and uploads to Cloudinary.

**Next step:** Poll `GET /jobs/:jobId` every 3–5 seconds until `status === "completed"`.

> **Tip:** Pass `originalFilename` (e.g. `"Building.rvt"`) from your upload step for best
> 2D/3D detection accuracy. Without it, the system still detects via APS manifest analysis.

put.summary: Step 2 — Bulk upsert takeoff elements of a given type
put.description:
**Save the spreadsheet data for one element type tab.**

Accepts an array of elements and upserts them into the project. Elements are
identified by the compound key `(projectId + elementType + elementId)`. If an
element with the same `elementId` already exists for this type, it is updated;
otherwise it is inserted.

### What happens
1. Validates each element against shape-specific dimension rules.
2. Performs a MongoDB `bulkWrite` with upsert operations.
3. Returns the count of newly inserted vs. updated elements.

### Usage pattern
- Call this whenever the user saves a tab in the takeoff spreadsheet.
- The frontend groups elements by `elementType` (one tab per type).
- Maximum **500 elements** per request.
- `elementCategory` is auto-derived from `elementType` on the server side.

---

## Payload variations by `elementType`

Every element accepts the **base fields** below. Additional fields are
relevant only for specific element-type families and are ignored by the
calculation engine for other types.

### Base fields (all element types)
| Field             | Type     | Required                              | Notes |
|-------------------|----------|---------------------------------------|-------|
| `elementId`       | string   | yes                                   | User label e.g. C1, ES1, GB2 |
| `shape`           | enum     | yes                                   | `rectangular` \| `circular` |
| `count`           | integer  | no (default 1)                        | Repetition multiplier — UI "No. Thus" cell |
| `nr`              | number   | no                                    | Extra multiplier (multiplied with `count`) |
| `length`          | number   | for `rectangular`                     | metres — also used as "Length/Radius" cell on shapes that share it |
| `width`           | number   | for `rectangular`                     | metres |
| `depth`           | number   | required wherever a height is needed  | metres |
| `diameter`        | number   | for `circular`                        | metres |
| `height`          | number   | for columns, walls, lift shaft        | metres — UI "Height (m)" column |
| `thickness`       | number   | for slabs, walls, lift shaft          | metres — overrides `depth` for slab/wall families |
| `floorThickness`  | number   | for beams (Floor & Beam › Beam tab)   | metres — UI "Floor Thickness" column |
| `floorLabel`      | string   | when row belongs to a non-default floor | One of `getFloors()` output: `GROUND_FLOOR`, `FLOOR_1`…`FLOOR_N`, `ROOF`, `LIFT_SHAFT`, `EXTERNAL`. Part of the unique key together with `(project, elementType, elementId)` so the **same** `elementId` can repeat per floor. |
| `areaReference`   | string   | no                                    | Free-text e.g. "Site A" |
| `state`           | enum     | no                                    | `isolated` \| `continuous` — applies to columns and foundations |
| `reinforcement`   | array    | no                                    | Bar schedule rows (atomic per-bar) |
| `layeredReinforcement` | array | no                                  | Layered bar schedule rows (4-box UI mapping — see Reinforcement-tab note below) |

### Reinforcement sub-tab — 4-box convention (Column, Beam, Pad Footing)
The Reinforcement sub-tab on **Column**, **Beam**, and **Pad Footing** pages renders 4 small
input boxes per cell. Those 4 boxes map 1-to-1 to indices `[0]…[3]` of every array on
a single `layeredReinforcement` entry:

| Box index | Bar group  |
|-----------|------------|
| `[0]`     | Bottom-X   |
| `[1]`     | Bottom-Y   |
| `[2]`     | Top-X      |
| `[3]`     | Top-Y      |

All arrays on the entry (`centerToCenter`, `sizeDia`, `noThus`, `noInEach`, `cutLength`)
MUST be the same length and aligned by index. Send `0` for empty boxes — never shorten
the array. See the `pad_footing`, `column_with_reinforcement`, and
`beam_with_floor_thickness_and_reinforcement` examples below.

### Element-type families and their extra fields

| Family / `elementType`(s) | Extra fields used | Calculation produced |
|---|---|---|
| **Columns / Pads / Pile caps** — `column`, `column_in_foundation`, `column_footing`, `pad_footing`, `pile_cap`, `pile_cap_frames`, `roof_column` | `height`, `state` (`isolated`/`continuous`), `floorLabel`, `diameter` (when `shape: circular`), `layeredReinforcement` (4-box) | concrete volume + formwork |
| **Beams** — `beam`, `ground_beam`, `lintels`, `roof_beam` | `depth`, `floorThickness`, `floorLabel`, `layeredReinforcement` (4-box) | concrete volume + beam formwork |
| **Slabs** — `slab`, `raft_foundation`, `oversite_slab`, `ground_floor_bed`, `kitchen_countertop`, `water_slab`, `roof_slab`, `staircase_landing`, `parapet_wall_copping` | `thickness` (overrides `depth`), `floorLabel` (for upper-floor slabs) | concrete volume + slab formwork |
| **Walls** — `wall`, `shear_wall`, `lift_wall`, `parapet_wall` | `thickness`, `height` (alias for depth), `floorLabel` | concrete volume + wall formwork |
| **Lift shaft** — `lift_shaft` | `length`, `width`, `height`, `thickness`, `floorLabel: "LIFT_SHAFT"` | concrete volume + wall formwork (treated as a vertical enclosure) |
| **Strip foundation** — `strip_foundation` | base only | concrete volume + beam-style formwork |
| **Pile** — `pile` | base only (use `diameter` for circular) | concrete volume only |
| **Excavation (no concrete)** — `excavation_clearing`, `excavation_strip`, `excavation_ground_beam` | base `length`, `width`, `depth`. UI helper inputs (`stripThickness`, `numberOfBranches`, `colBLength`, `colBWidth`, `pitDepth`, `blockworkWidth`, `blockworkHeight`) may be stored for round-tripping but the engine reads only `length`/`width`/`depth` | excavation volume |
| **DDT / void deductions** — `ddt_pad_pit_in_strip`, `upper_floor_ddt_void`, `ground_floor_bed_void` | base `length`, `width`, `depth` + `floorLabel` (for `upper_floor_ddt_void`). Helper inputs same as excavation family may be saved (`stripThickness`, `numberOfBranches`, `colBLength`, `colBWidth`, `pitDepth`, `blockworkWidth`, `blockworkHeight`, `areaToBeDeducted`) | **negative** concrete volume |
| **Strip length calculator** — `strip_length_calculator` | helper inputs only — `numberOfBranches`, `lin`, `colBLength`, `colBWidth` (used UI-side to derive `length`); resulting `length`/`width`/`depth` should still be sent | concrete volume + beam formwork |
| **Filling / floor build-ups** — fields `fillingThickness`, `floorThickness`, `stripThickness` are accepted for substructure rows but ignored by the core calculator | — | — |
| **Pile counts** — `numberOfPiles` is accepted for pile-related rows | — | — |
| **Swimming pool / staircases** — `swimming_pool`, `staircase`, `staircase_strings_steps`, `staircase_upper_floors` | base only — fallback rectangular/circular volume | concrete volume + formwork |

> **Note:** All extra fields are persisted as-is on the `TakeoffElement`
> so the UI can re-hydrate the spreadsheet exactly as the user typed it.
> The calculation engine, however, only reads the geometric fields
> documented above for each family. For the **Strip Foundation page →
> Excavation (Strip) → Ddt Pad_Pit In Strip** sub-tab, the frontend
> should compute `length`/`width`/`depth` from the visible helper
> inputs (Strip Thickness, No. of Branches, Col. B Length/Width, Pit
> Depth, Blockwork Width/Height) before submitting, and may also send
> the helper inputs themselves so they survive a reload.

or continue adding more element types.

post.summary: Step 6 — Commit calculation and generate BOQ
post.description:
**The "Generate BOQ" button — final step of the manual takeoff flow.**

Fetches **all saved** takeoff elements for the project, runs the full
calculation engine, converts results into a structured BOQ (Bill of
Quantities) grouped by `elementCategory`, and persists it as the
project's `boqResult`. This is the terminal action.

### What happens
1. Loads every saved `TakeoffElement` for this project from the DB.
2. Runs the calculation engine (concrete, formwork, rebar) on each.
3. Groups the per-element results into BOQ sections by
   `elementCategory` (e.g. Substructure, Superstructure).
4. **Enriches BOQ rows with library pricing** — if the project has
   linked library items, each row is matched by description + unit
   and gets a `rate`, computed `amount` (quantity × rate), and a
   `librarySnapshot` with the matched item's details.
5. Persists the enriched BOQ as `project.boqResult`.
6. Returns both the persisted `boqResult` and the raw
   `CalculationSummary` for display.

### Prerequisites
- The project must have **at least one saved takeoff element** (via
  **Step 2** — Bulk Upsert).
- Ensure elements are up-to-date — unsaved spreadsheet edits will NOT
  be included. Save first, then commit.
- For pricing, link **library items** to the project beforehand.
  Rows whose description + unit match a library item will receive
  the item's `finalRate`. Unmatched rows keep `rate: 0`.

### Usage pattern
- Wire to the "Generate BOQ" / "Commit" button.
- After commit, redirect the user to the BOQ viewer page.

### Previous step
- **Step 5** — Preview calculation (optional live feedback)

Saves the entire takeoff workspace in a single request: a list of
element-type *groups*, each with its own array of elements. Designed
for **autosave** flows where the client owns the canonical workspace
state and pushes the full snapshot.

**Flow / steps**
1. Server validates the payload (1–50 groups; each group 1–500 elements).
2. For every group, it delegates to the standard `bulkUpsertElements`
   path, so all existing `qsProjectType` and structural-scope
   constraints (e.g., disallowed element types per project type) are
   enforced unchanged.
3. Upserts use the compound key
   `{ projectId, elementType, elementId, floorLabel }` — meaning the
   same `elementId` can legally repeat across floors.
4. Returns aggregated counters across all groups.

**Idempotency / overwrite semantics**
This endpoint *upserts*; it does not delete elements that are absent
from the payload. To remove an element, call the dedicated DELETE
endpoint or DELETE-by-type endpoint.

Requires authentication. Any authenticated user can fetch any user profile.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The 24-character MongoDB ObjectId of the user.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid JWT token.

put.description:
Updates one or more fields of a user's profile. All fields in the request body
are optional — only the provided fields will be updated. An audit log entry is
created for every successful update. Cached user data is invalidated.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The 24-character MongoDB ObjectId of the user to update.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid JWT token.
